name: Cinematic Video Hero
summary: A full-viewport muted video loop is treated as an opening film shot — real-time footage as the base plane with staged type assembling over it. The premium tell is restraint: film-grade footage, a legibility scrim, and one disciplined accent instead of effects.

composition: Asymmetric split: subject anchored to one side, headline stack over confident negative space on the other — magazine-cover balance, never centered-on-face.
A fixed cinematic frame (eyebrow, title zone, index/labels, controls) that any footage pours into — the chrome is the constant, the film is the variable.
Minimal nav; the frame should feel like a title card, not a website header.
layering: Footage as the full-bleed background plane → a soft gradient/vignette scrim for legibility → type and UI on the frontmost plane.
Depth comes from the footage's own camera work and depth-of-field, not stacked cutouts.
An optional info/caption layer can toggle away so the media can be viewed clean.
lighting: Light is the footage's own cinematography; the only added light is a radial gradient lifting the headline zone off the film.
Desaturated or monochrome grades unify disparate clips; the grade is the brand.
typography: Film-title typography: high-end serif display for luxury registers or engineered sans for tech; small tracked support copy.
Type assembles ONTO the running film — title first, support second, CTA last — then holds; the elegance is in stillness over motion.

rules: Let the footage own the color; interface chrome stays neutral/dark so any clip drops in without clashing.
One restrained accent (a gold outline, a single violet) owns 100% of the non-photographic saturation and points at the primary action.

easing: The motion is the footage itself, playing at real-world pace; overlay text uses long gentle fades/rises with expo-out settles.
No bounce, no spring — anything springy breaks the film register.
pacing: Unhurried: text settles once and holds; transitions between media run ~1s film-trailer crossfades.
The loop must be seamless — a visible loop seam reads as cheap instantly.
choreography: Video plays continuously as the base layer; on load the title, subhead, and CTA stagger in over the still-running film.
In gallery form: media crossfades first, then title and index labels re-reveal — footage always leads, type follows.

gapNotes: No video-texture plane primitive in the prism runtime — hub backgrounds are procedural/3D presets; a video-loop background layer (muted, autoplaying, seamless-loop, reduced-motion-aware) does not exist yet.
No generative video model is wired into the capability family (image and 3D only), so 'footage without user upload' has no path — W-PHOTO or a future gen-video adapter must decide the source.
Legibility scrim + LUT grade over a video layer needs the R1 cinematic floor post stack (W-PHOTO).

whenToUse: Portfolio/showreel, hospitality, film, and quiet-luxury brands where footage already exists or is being produced.
Any brief whose product is inherently in motion (venues, performance, food preparation, travel).
whenNotToUse: Bandwidth-sensitive or accessibility-first contexts — autoplay full-bleed video is heavy and must degrade to a poster frame.
Content-dense pages needing fast scanning; the film pace delays information.
When only stock-feeling footage is available — weak film reads worse than a strong still.

notes: Pairs with glitch-cyber-fx only as its transition language (footage between glitch bursts); never run a GPU field over playing footage.
The monochrome + single-metallic-accent pairing (see quiet-luxury-monochrome) is the strongest observed premium register for this family.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as scroll-video-scrub and media-showreel-gallery — all footage-led surfaces.
